findings.description: SWR-DIA-001 requires each applicable fault report within 10 ms. SWC-SUP-039 calculates that four simultaneous reports behind an answer line can take up to 12.9 ms. OP-SWC-013 records the unresolved requirement-level decision.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the interaction between report deadlines and an answer already in progress, then specify an architecture that satisfies the resulting requirement.

findings.description: The flow check is performed at the end of the 10 ms cycle, but T_DIAG has a 20 ms execution limit and may not yet have supplied its checkpoint. OP-SWC-011 identifies the unresolved interpretation of SWR-FLW-001.
findings.requested_change: Resolve when T_DIAG's checkpoint must be evaluated and make the flow-check sequence consistent with that decision.

findings.description: The diagnostic task runs below the application tasks, yet SWC-SUP-039 assumes it runs within 1 ms of a report submission. SWC-SUP-061 supplies no application execution or scheduling bound that guarantees this response; T_DIAG alone has a 20 ms execution limit.
findings.requested_change: Specify and justify scheduling and response-time bounds that let diagnostic transmission meet the applicable report and service deadlines under the permitted application workload.

findings.description: DEC-SWC-013 now allocates 920 µs per 10 ms cycle, but the budgets are unverified targets and OP-SWC-012 leaves the core clock and CRC throughput to detailed design. The architecture does not establish that the 500 µs CRC segment and remaining work can be achieved on the configured platform.
findings.requested_change: Provide an architecture-level basis for the execution allocations and their feasibility at the configured core clock, or identify the unresolved platform decision as a blocking open point.

findings.description: The scheduler represents configured periods as whole 10 ms tick counts, but SWC-SUP-001 validates only zero periods, unknown tasks and limits longer than periods. OP-SWC-005 leaves non-integral periods and their validation unresolved, so accepted configuration data need not have the timing it specifies.
findings.requested_change: Define and validate the supported period range and tick granularity, or obtain the necessary configuration decision before accepting such data.
